intro: Aaron Judge, the six-foot-seven right fielder for the New York Yankees, owns the American League record of 62 home runs, set in 2022, and has collected three AL MVP trophies. A rib stress fracture limited him to 66 games in 2026, yet he still managed 18 homers and an .871 OPS. Once healthy, he went deep in the Sept. 14 victory that locked up a playoff spot.

jerseyPoints.label: The number
jerseyPoints.text: No. 99 is a number almost nobody in baseball wears, so it belongs to Judge alone and is impossible to mistake.

jerseyPoints.label: The pinstripes
jerseyPoints.text: The Yankees' home look has barely changed in a century and still carries no names on the back, so the number does all the talking.

jerseyPoints.label: The captaincy
jerseyPoints.text: Captain since late 2022 and the face of the franchise for years, Judge is a lasting pick rather than a one-season trend.

jerseyPoints.label: The power
jerseyPoints.text: Few hitters produce more jaw-dropping home runs, and his jersey is a tribute to that raw strength.

closing: If you want one baseball jersey that will still feel current a decade from now, the Judge No. 99 is a safe bet.

closing: For Red Sox fans excited about a new leader behind the plate, the Rutschman No. 31 is the jersey to grab.

jerseyPoints.label: The number

jerseyPoints.label: The colors

jerseyPoints.label: The record

closing: If you want a hockey jersey with true historic weight, the Ovechkin No. 8 is the one to own.
